title: Vite multi-page site pre-rendered to static HTML at build time
notes:
A clean control, and the discriminating half of a pair. This fixture and react-spa declare the same React dependencies and the same Vite build tool, and the profiler reports a JavaScript framework for both. The difference is in the bytes: here each route is its own HTML entry whose head is authored by hand, and the build renders the body into the document before it is written to dist/, so the served page is complete. react-spa ships an empty shell and assembles the page in the browser. Every finding on react-spa and no finding here is the evidence that the checks read captured output rather than the dependency list - which is the property that makes the whole registry defensible, because a rule that fired on package.json would be guessing.

The home page is captured twice, once as served and once after its inline script ran, so content-in-initial-html and client-mutates-canonical actually run and actually pass. That script is progressive enhancement and nothing else: it marks the root element and expands a build stamp by seven words. content-in-initial-html only reports when the initial response carries less than half the final text and at least a hundred words are missing, so this page - 222 words served, 229 after execution - is the case that proves the threshold is not hair-trigger. A fixture where those two checks reported NOT_APPLICABLE would prove nothing about either, and one where they fired on a complete document would be a false positive.

The other two routes are captured once. A comparison that was never made is not a comparison that passed, so those routes contribute nothing to either JavaScript-rendering check.

raw_html_path names dist/*.html rather than the source entries at the fixture root, because the built document is what a reader receives; the entries still carry their <!--app-html--> placeholder and any line number pointed at them would be precise and wrong.

Four checks report NOT_APPLICABLE because the fixture declares no hreflang alternates and carries no review or rating markup. Those are absent from expected_non_findings on purpose: the false-positive rate divides by the number of checks that genuinely inspected something, and padding that denominator with checks which never looked would flatter the number.
expected_not_applicable_rationale: A documentation site for a toolchain. It has no catalogue, no submissions, one language, no entitlement, and no faceted navigation, so none of these can be satisfied without inventing the thing they describe.
expected_applicable_rationale: The two JavaScript-rendering rules are the discriminating pair. They are gated on client_rendered or javascript_app, and this project declares React and Vite, so they must be offered here exactly as they are on react-spa - and then pass, because the bytes are complete. A selector that skipped them here would make the react-spa findings unfalsifiable, since a rule that is never offered can never be wrong. The other three are gated on facts this fixture deliberately establishes by shipping a sitemap and a feed; asserting them keeps the fixture honest about why those files exist.
